newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai fin. minister to hold news conference Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Thai fin. minister to hold news conference Tuesday.

text.p: Thai finance minister Thanong Bidaya said on Tuesday he would hold a news conference after the cabinet discusses a proposed package of economic measures recommended by the IMF.
Thanong would not say what time the news conference would be. He made the comments as he and prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh headed into the cabinet meeting around 0245 GMT.
Cabinet meetings are usually completed shortly after midday (0500 GMT). Chavalit told reporters this meeting was expected to be longer than usual.

Thanong said on Monday he would unveil the framework of the IMF-sponsored package to the cabinet on Tuesday. He said no loan details had been worked out but he would seek cabinet approval for the basic framework of the package.

The austerity package is expected to include a series of stiff monetary and fiscal measures, and a reform of the debt-ridden financial and property sectors. One of the more hotly-contested items supported by the IMF but initially opposed by the Thai government was an expected increase in the value-added tax, local media reported.

Analysts have said Thailand needs about $10-$20 billion to get the ailing economy back on an even keel. The country has nearly $90 billion in foreign currency debt, about $40 billion of which is short-term and comes due within one year.

Japan's Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper reported on Tuesday that the IMF, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), Japan's Export-Import Bank and Japanese commercial banks will provide a total of $10 billion to support Thailand's economy.

Quoting international financial sources, the paper said the IMF and the ADB would together provide $5 billion to the rescue package, while the Ex-Im Bank is expected to match whatever contribution the IMF makes.
An international monetary source later said Japan's package was not expected to be unveiled on Tuesday.
